evidence.s1_ci: ci.yml runs on pull_request and push to main. It runs `npm ci`, `npm test` and `npm run build` in site/; these scripts exist in site/package.json, the repo's only package.json. A final step checks that the working tree is still clean. The workflow-level permissions are `contents: read`. pages.yml grants `pages: write`/`id-token: write` only on the deploy job. release.yml uses `contents: write`, which a release needs. The only token used is GITHUB_TOKEN (`GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}`), and there is no pull_request_target. However, every action uses a tag rather than a full commit SHA (`actions/checkout@v4`, `setup-node@v4`, `configure-pages@v5`, `upload-pages-artifact@v3`, `deploy-pages@v4`: step1.patch lines 91, 93, 155, 165, 181, 197, 228), which fails an explicit requirement. pages.yml also has `workflow_dispatch` with no ref guard, so the workflow itself does not limit deploys to main. Nothing was pushed or run, and step 1 did not touch app code, tests or data.
evidence.s1_readme: The README (step1.patch lines 466-552) covers: clone and `npm ci` with Node 22 from .nvmrc; `npm run dev`; `npm test`; running one test with `npx vitest run src/lib/router.test.ts`; `npx svelte-check --tsconfig ./tsconfig.json`; `npm run build`/`preview`; PAGES_BASE; prepare-data/index/fieldsets/sample-bullets; contributing data (linked to CONTRIBUTING.md#contributing-data and the existing issue forms); commit convention; releases; and the MIT license. Every script exists in site/package.json, as do site/tsconfig.json, site/scripts/sample-bullets.ts, LICENSE, THIRD-PARTY.md and data/bullets/README.md. vite.config.ts:11 reads PAGES_BASE. The generated files the docs name are in site/.gitignore.
evidence.s1_release: The strategy holds together: the version is in site/package.json (0.1.0), and a release is made by a `chore(release): vX.Y.Z` commit plus an annotated tag. release.yml checks that the tag matches package.json, that the commit is on main and that the changelog section is not empty, then publishes that section and a data tarball. CHANGELOG.md states Keep a Changelog 1.1.0 and SemVer. Dependabot covers npm in /site and github-actions. CONTRIBUTING.md states Conventional Commits, and all 7 commits in commits.txt follow it. Two small inconsistencies: CONTRIBUTING says tooling and docs changes need no changelog entry, yet the Unreleased section lists CI, Dependabot and README entries. CONTRIBUTING also maps dependencies to the `build` type, but dependabot.yml uses the `chore(deps)` prefix for npm.
evidence.s2_requirements: Every requirement is met. Route: router.ts parses `compare/<a>/<b>` with decoding, and href.compare builds the URL. SVG: role=img, aria-label `Profiles of {a} and {b}` using the records' names, one `<path>` per outline. Shot cartridges are excluded in outlineOf. Table: `<caption>` `Dimensions (mm|in)`; headers `Symbol`, the two names and `Difference`; symbols from FIELD_LABELS; Tol fields and FIELD_UNITS fields excluded; only the cartridge part is read. Difference is B−A. Units follow unitSystem() and use formatValue or displayNumber(…,'in'). CompareWith.svelte gives a `Compare with` label tied to a NativeSelect listing the other entries, and a `Compare` submit button that sets `#/compare/<key>/<target>`. German strings are in i18n.svelte.ts. Tests, a changelog entry and a commit are there.
evidence.s2_correctness: overlay() builds one viewportFor over both caseOuterProfile results (z measured from the head face), so both share one scale, the axis at xy(0,0)[0] and the head face at xy(0,0)[1]. fullSectionPath gives a single closed path per case. dimensionsOf skips non-numbers, `*Tol` fields, FIELD_UNITS fields (pressures, angles, N) and repeating groups (shotshell). A metric difference is cleaned of float noise with toPrecision(12), matching displayNumber, so 11.96−11.53 shows 0.43. An imperial difference converts the mm difference, not two rounded values. Unknown keys and undrawable records (shotshell, records missing the rim) get messages. I found no wrong values.
evidence.s2_fit: It reuses lib/core (FIELD_LABELS, FIELD_UNITS, GROUP_ORDER, orderedFields, formatValue), lib/shapes2d (adaptMetallic, caseOuterProfile), lib/geom (viewportFor, fullSectionPath), site units.ts/units.svelte.ts, data.ts byKey/load, PageLoadError and the shadcn Button/Label/NativeSelect. It follows the existing lazy-chunk routing, the `data-ui` + `@layer legacy` style pattern and metadata.ts. Small duplications: compare.ts:333-334 re-implements orderedGroups from site/src/lib/fields.ts, the table CSS copies GroupTable's rules instead of sharing them, and the `compare.failed` string is unused. The test imports fixtures by a relative path.
evidence.s2_tests: compare.test.ts reads the real 308 Win., 300 Win. Mag., 12 and 7x67 R records. It covers dimension extraction (symbols, excluded units, Tol and angles, ordering, repeating groups), the shared-row logic, metric and imperial formatting, the sign of B−A, outline reuse equal to caseOuterProfile, nulls for shot cartridges and incomplete records, and overlay geometry (head line, common axis, scale ratio, bounds). router.test.ts gains route parsing, round-trip and invalid-URL cases. No test covers the Svelte layer (SVG accessible name, caption/headers, CompareWith, German strings), but the repo has no component tests, so this follows its setup.
evidence.s3_fixes: Bug: compareRows now returns the union with optional a/b. Compare.svelte leaves value and Difference cells empty when a figure is missing. A test checks `delta L` (308 only) and `R3` (300 WM only) from the real data. Style: th and td in the three figure columns get `.figure { text-align: right }`. The step 2 CSS already had `[data-ui=Compare] th, td { text-align: right }` with first-child set to left, so the new rule is redundant but harmless. The lede, the empty-table text and the changelog were changed to match the new behaviour. The insertion order puts symbols only B publishes after B's predecessor, which can break the detail page's group order: the test expects L1, L3, H1, L2, with lengths symbol L2 after collar symbol H1.
evidence.cross_step: Step 2 added an Unreleased/Added changelog entry. Step 3 amended that unreleased entry, which is correct under Keep a Changelog for a feature not yet released. The version stays 0.1.0, which matches the stated strategy of bumping only at release time. The commits `feat(site): compare two cartridges` and `fix(site): list every dimension either cartridge publishes in compare` follow the convention. The code type-checks by inspection (ES2022 target for Object.hasOwn, optional fields guarded in the template), and a built site/dist containing the Compare chunk exists.

unmet_requirements: Step 1 (review criterion): GitHub Actions are pinned to version tags (@v4, @v5, @v3), not full commit SHAs.
strengths: The compare view meets every requirement in step 2. It is built on the shared libraries (caseOuterProfile, viewportFor/fullSectionPath, FIELD_LABELS/FIELD_UNITS/orderedFields, formatValue, displayNumber), so the profiles and values are exactly the ones the detail page uses.

Step 1's strategy holds together and is checked in CI: the version is in site/package.json, a tag-triggered release refuses a tag that disagrees with package.json, main or the changelog, the changelog uses Keep a Changelog, and Conventional Commits is followed in every commit.
The tests read the real records, including the delta L and R3 cases from the step 3 comment, and check the overlay geometry, the unit conversion and the sign of the difference.
issues: None of the workflows pins its actions to full commit SHAs; all use tags such as actions/checkout@v4. This is a supply-chain risk for a repository that takes outside pull requests.

In step 3, symbols only the second cartridge publishes are placed after its predecessor in that cartridge's own order, which can break the detail page's group order (the test expects lengths symbol L2 after collar symbol H1). The alignment fix duplicates a right-align rule the step 2 CSS already had.

Small inconsistencies: dimensionsOf re-implements orderedGroups, the compare.failed string is unused, the CHANGELOG lists tooling entries that CONTRIBUTING says need none, and dependabot's `chore(deps)` prefix contradicts the `build` type for dependencies.
review.verdict: The compare feature and its step 3 fix are correct, reuse the shared libraries well and are well tested, and the release, changelog and commit conventions are followed in every step. The main problem is that none of the workflows pins its actions to commit SHAs, alongside small ordering and duplication issues; I would merge after pinning the actions.
